summary: The settlement stall is best explained by a schema-contract break introduced by order-service v2.16.0 (dep-6010, 07:40Z), which renamed the OrderExecuted field qty→quantity and emitted a schema v2 header while settlement-service's consumer still expects schema v1; the first v2-shaped message on orders-3 (@8841207) failed to deserialize at 07:42:14Z, was retried as a poison message, and permanently blocked the partition, so lag climbed monotonically to 60k+ and throughput collapsed. Confidence is medium (0.72 per the reviewed ranking): the failing log line, the 07:40Z deploy, and the lag/request_rate onset are tightly coincident, and the only alternative with a real change (the 07:35Z poll-batch setting cfg-3004) cannot mechanically produce schema errors. The residual uncertainty is confined to a hop no available tool can verify — no explicit topic→partition mapping and no produce-side timestamp — so the message's producer identity is inferred from the exact field-rename match and the deploy→first-error ordering rather than proven. Recommended path: keep the poison offset from blocking the partition (DLQ/skip or roll the producer back), then align the consumer contract to schema v2.

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2.16.0 schema rename (qty→quantity) breaks settlement-service deserialization; poison message blocks orders-3
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The order-service v2.16.0 deploy (dep-6010, 07:40Z) changed the OrderExecuted event contract: it renamed field `qty` to `quantity` and began emitting a schema v2 header. settlement-service's consumer still expects schema v1 with a required `qty` field (its code/config was frozen since before March — no deploys), so the first v2-shaped OrderExecuted message on orders-3 (offset 8841207) fails to deserialize at 07:42:14Z; it is treated as a poison message and retried indefinitely, permanently blocking partition orders-3. Consumption stalls (request_rate 62→0.4 req/s), lag climbs monotonically to 60k+ while order-service keeps producing, and zero settlements post. The exact topic->partition mapping is not exposed by tooling, but the message content (v2 header + missing qty, exactly the field dep-6010 renamed) and the 07:40Z→07:42:14Z ordering make the dep-6010 producer the only credible origin.

causal_chain.claim: order-service v2.16.0 deployed 07:40Z, renaming OrderExecuted field qty->quantity and setting event schema version header v2 (dep-6010)
order-service is a producer on the shared kafka broker; settlement-service consumes from that same broker, so order-service's OrderExecuted stream reaches settlement-service's consumer
settlement-service's consumer contract was not changed in this window (zero deploys since 2026-03-01), so it still expects schema v1 with required field qty

First message to carry the v2 shape on orders-3 (offset 8841207) fails deserialization: 'missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' — the payload is v2-shaped, hitting a v1-expecting deserializer
The failed message is retried as a poison message, blocking partition orders-3 (196 poison-retry ERRORs, first 07:44:51Z, same offset through 09:58Z)

Consumption stalls: request_rate collapses 62->0.4 req/s and consumer_lag climbs monotonically from ~26 at 07:41 to 60220 avg by 09:55Z; onset 07:42 is exactly when the poison offset is first consumed
Symptom: zero settlements posted (not a 5xx wave — error_rate flat ~0.1-0.32%); lag keeps growing as order-service continues producing v2 events

assumptions: settlement-service consumes specifically the topic/partition that order-service produces; tooling exposes no topic->partition mapping (only the literal 'orders-3' in the consumer's own error log), so this hop is inferred, not verified.

The poison message's payload originates from the post-07:40Z order-service v2.16.0 producer: no produce-side timestamp exists (F29), so this rests on the 6.5-min deploy->first-error gap plus the exact field-rename match, not on a message-level producer identity.
The v1 schema pin is a pre-existing consumer contract (only visible in runtime error text, not declared in config metadata), and settlement-service was never updated to accept v2/quantity.
order-service had no throughput drop at 07:40Z (its error_rate and logs are clean; throughput unverified due to budget exhaustion — F18).

ranked_hypotheses.title: settlement-service consumer poll-settings change (max.poll.records 500→200) stalled consumption
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The config change cfg-3004 shrinking max.poll.records to 200 on settlement-service (07:35:37Z, 'smaller poll batches to smooth DB writes') altered poll pacing or commit behavior, slowing or stalling the consumer so settlements stopped posting and lag accrued. This is the reporter's suspicion.

causal_chain.claim: max.poll.records changed 500->200 on settlement-service at 07:35:37Z by m.das
Smaller poll batches slow processing and/or alter offset commit timing, possibly triggering rebalance-timeout stalls
Consumption throughput collapses and lag grows from ~07:42Z

assumptions: Reducing poll batch size can produce a total, sustained stall rather than merely slower processing.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Mechanism mismatch: the observed failures are deserialization errors ('missing required field qty', 'schema v1 expected, header says v2') plus explicit 'poison message ... partition blocked' errors pinned to a single offset (F14, F25, F26, F27). A poll batch-size change cannot produce schema errors, a renamed-field failure, or a hard partition block. Timing is also non-specific: the config landed 07:35Z but lag/errors start only at 07:42Z — right after the 07:40Z deploy. No historical precedent links poll settings to lag (F12), though that absence rests on limited keyword searches.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared kafka broker partition-assignment loss / rebalancing storm stalls settlement consumer
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A broker-side event (partition reassignment / rebalancing storm) on the shared kafka broker caused settlement-service's consumer to lose its partition assignment, halting consumption and accruing lag — the HIST-112/HIST-104 pattern.

causal_chain.claim: Shared kafka broker suffers a partition reassignment / rebalance storm
settlement-service consumer loses its partition assignment
Consumption stops and lag grows from ~07:42Z

assumptions: Broker-side reassignment occurred at ~07:40-07:42Z; no broker telemetry was available to observe it.
The Feb/Nov historical pattern recurs with no triggering deploy.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Rests only on historical precedent (HIST-112/HIST-104, F7/F8 — past incidents, weak evidence) with no positive telemetry: no broker partition-assignment/reassignment metrics or group-state events were queried, and the dismissal is by inference rather than direct falsification (critic's minor note acknowledged). Critically, the observed signatures are deserialization/poison errors on one specific offset with content that exactly matches the 07:40Z deploy's field rename (F14, F25, F26, F27) — a schema-contract failure, not an assignment loss. A partition-assignment loss would not produce 'missing required field qty ... header says v2'.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared ledger-db or broker contention throttles settlement-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Contention on the shared ledger-db (four services) or the shared broker throttled settlement-service's consumption/writes, stalling settlements; settlement is merely where the symptom surfaced.

causal_chain.claim: ledger-db (shared by order-, portfolio-, payment-, settlement-service) becomes contended
settlement-service writes to ledger-db stall, blocking processing

assumptions: DB or broker contention began at exactly 07:40-07:42Z with no triggering change.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: No telemetry shows DB or broker saturation (cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, latency queries were budget-exhausted; nothing positive was found). The observed errors are schema/deserialization errors unrelated to write contention, and F14/F26/F27 explain the hard, single-offset block directly without invoking shared-resource throttling. Note the reporter's own config rationale ('smoothing DB writes') hints at DB pressure, but no evidence supports contention as the origin.

timeline.event: Config change cfg-3004 applied on settlement-service: consumer.max.poll.records 500→200 (by m.das, 'smaller poll batches to smooth DB writes').
Only deploy of the window: order-service v2.16.0 ('Order events v2') goes live, renaming OrderExecuted field qty→quantity and adding event schema header v2. Not rolled back.
settlement-service consumer_lag still low (26.25) — last pre-onset bucket.
Lag onset: consumer_lag jumps to 386.63 (07:42 bucket avg 603.29 vs 31.06 at 07:40); request_rate collapses from ~62 req/s to ~0.4 req/s and stays there.
First deserialize ERROR on orders-3@8841207: 'missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' — a v2-shaped message blocking a v1-expecting consumer.
Lag continues climbing (1516 at 07:44); first poison-message retry logged at 07:44:51Z ('retrying orders-3@8841207 ..., partition blocked').
Lag reaches 6028 and continues rising monotonically as order-service keeps producing.
Incident INC-010 reported by on-call SRE: no settlements posted for ~40 minutes, settlement consumer lag growing.
Lag reaches avg 60220.76 / max 61605.53; HTTP error_rate remains flat at ~0.2%, confirming the symptom is a throughput stall not a 5xx spike.
Offset orders-3@8841207 still failing/blocked (last_match) — the poison message has not cleared.

recommended_actions.action: Unblock the poison offset on partition orders-3 (offset 8841207) on settlement-service: route the failing message to a dead-letter topic / skip it using the consumer's poison-message handling (or, if DLQ is not configurable, raise the consumer's max retries and skip-on-deserialize-failure), then restart the settlement-service consumer group so consumption resumes on orders-3.
recommended_actions.rationale: The partition is hard-blocked by a single retried offset (F14, F25, F27) and lag is climbing monotonically to 60k+ (F13, F28); clearing the blocked offset is the direct mitigation and matches the HIST-112 fix pattern for stalled consumers (F7).

recommended_actions.action: In parallel, roll back order-service to the pre-dep-6010 version (stop emitting schema v2 / quantity OrderExecuted events) or pause the v2.16.0 producer path, to halt the injection of further messages the settlement consumer cannot deserialize.
recommended_actions.rationale: dep-6010 is the only deploy in the window and it changed exactly the contract that is failing (F1, F10, F23, F26); rolling back removes the source of incompatible messages while the consumer is fixed.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT revert cfg-3004 (consumer.max.poll.records=200) as the first action; leave it at 200 pending the schema fix.
recommended_actions.rationale: A poll batch-size change cannot produce schema/deserialization errors or a hard partition block (F14, F25, F26, F27), the config landed 6.5 minutes before onset while lag/errors start only after the 07:40Z deploy (F2, F9, F17, F13), and there is no historical precedent for a poll-setting-caused lag incident (F12). Reverting it wastes mitigation time.

recommended_actions.action: Confirm recovery: verify consumer_lag on settlement-service returns to the pre-incident baseline (tens of messages) and request_rate recovers to ~62 req/s after the offset is cleared, and confirm settlements begin posting.
recommended_actions.rationale: Onset was measured as lag 26→386 in the 07:41/07:42 buckets with request_rate 62→0.4 (F13, F15, F28); the inverse movement is the acceptance signal for the fix.

recommended_actions.action: Update settlement-service's consumer contract to schema v2: accept the renamed field quantity (v2 header) while remaining backward-compatible with v1 (qty), and add a config-declared schema version so the pin is explicit rather than implicit in runtime behavior.
recommended_actions.rationale: The consumer was never updated for v2 — zero settlement-service deploys since March (F24) — while the producer now emits v2 (F1, F23, F26); the contract mismatch is the root cause mechanism.

recommended_actions.action: Add schema-compatibility gating to the deploy pipeline: any producer change to an event contract (field rename, header/version bump) must be validated against registered consumers' declared schemas before rollout, and consumers must handle unknown/future schema versions gracefully (skip-to-DLQ instead of blocking a partition).
recommended_actions.rationale: The incident's failure mode is a producer-side contract change unilaterally breaking a downstream consumer with no gating and no poison-message escape hatch (F1, F14, F23, F26, F27).

recommended_actions.action: Alert on consumer-lag onset rate and on any 'poison message / partition blocked' log pattern for settlement-service, so a single stuck offset pages within minutes rather than ~40 minutes.
recommended_actions.rationale: Lag went from 26 to 386 within one 2-minute bucket and kept climbing for ~2.5 hours before being reported (F13, F28); the existing alerting relied on an HTTP error_rate that stayed flat at ~0.2% and never fired (F16).

data_gaps: No Kafka topic catalog or explicit topic→partition mapping is exposed by any available tool; get_service_dependencies returns only a service-level edge to the shared 'kafka' broker (F19, F20). The literal 'orders-3' is known only from the consumer's own error log (F21), so the claim that settlement-service consumes the partition order-service produces is inferred, not verified. This is the main limit on the conclusion.

No produce-side timestamp for offset orders-3@8841207 exists (F29, F30): INFO searches returned 0 matches for offsets on settlement-service and for 'quantity'/'produced' on order-service. Whether the poison message was PRODUCED after 07:40Z is therefore inferred from the deploy→first-error gap, not proven.

order-service throughput (request_rate) was never queried, and settlement-service cpu_pct/restarts/db_pool_in_use/latency_p99 returned 'budget_exhausted'; blast-radius testing of order-service is only partial (error_rate + logs clean, throughput unverified) (F18).

The settled/posted count was not directly queried; 'zero settlements' was assessed indirectly via request_rate collapse and poison/partition-block errors, so 'zero posted' vs 'merely slow' is not directly measured.

No broker telemetry (partition-assignment/reassignment metrics, consumer group state, broker events) was queried, so the HIST-112 broker-side pattern (F7, F8) is dismissed on the strength of the explicit deserialize/poison error text rather than affirmatively falsified.

Pre-window config changes (04:00–06:22Z) were not baselined (budget exhausted), though baseline deploys were confirmed zero (F3); no kafka-side broker config change could be verified in or before the window.

No other candidate services (other consumers/producers of the orders topic, schema registry) were checked around 07:35–07:42Z, so whether settlement-service is the sole affected service remains partly open.
No evidence retrieves a declared config artifact pinning the consumer to schema v1; the v1-pin is known only from runtime error text (assumption, not verified config).
order-service config changes were not retrieved, so whether the producer's topic/partition routing or keying changed alongside the schema rename is unconfirmed.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Broker telemetry showing a partition reassignment, consumer-group rebalance, or loss of partition assignment on orders-3 at ~07:40–07:42Z (the HIST-112 pattern) would move the origin from the schema-contract break to H3 (infrastructure/broker cause).

A produce-side timestamp or Kafka message metadata showing offset orders-3@8841207 was produced BEFORE the 07:40Z dep-6010 deploy (i.e. carrying a v1/qty payload from the old producer) would break the link between the failing message and the v2.16.0 schema rename.
Evidence that settlement-service actually consumes a different topic/partition than order-service produces would invalidate the order-service → settlement-service hop and reduce H1 to unsupported.
A known poll-setting mechanism that can cause sustained consumer stalls (or a precedent incident attributing lag to max.poll.records) would revive H2 as a co-cause or primary cause.
DB or broker saturation telemetry (cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, latency, kafka throttling) coinciding with the 07:40–07:42Z onset would support H4 (shared-resource contention) as the origin.
A settlement-service deploy or config change that updated its consumer to expect schema v2 (contradicting F24) would remove the contract mismatch as the mechanism.

Evidence that the failing messages are dropped instead of blocking the partition (i.e. no true poison-message partition block) would require re-explaining the lag and request_rate collapse on another basis.
